# BLO-37760 / BLO-37961 / BLO-38518 — prompt bundle and skill links resolve from both address spaces

Re-cut of [#2107](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2107) onto the BLO-32734 subPath work ([#2397](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2397)), whose own entry is `blo-32734.md`. These are the rows #2107 appended to the frozen `PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md` table, moved here verbatim (see [README.md](./README.md)): appending to that table is what ejected #1459 from the rebase merge queue.

| [BLO-37760](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-37760) | `src/server/prompt-cache.ts`, `src/server/prompt-cache.test.ts`, `src/server/execute.ts`, `src/server/execute.test.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts` | The sixth and last isolation root, and the one the BLO-32734 row above named as its known residual. `promptCacheRoot` is the only root with a **server-side writer**: `prepareClaudePromptBundle` `mkdir`s and writes the skills bundle in the paperclip process, then returns one string used as three things (write target, `--add-dir`, `--append-system-prompt-file`). That is coherent only while both mounts are `/paperclip`. Under a custom `config.workspaceMountPath` it wrote the bundle to the POD's address **on the server's own container filesystem** while handing the pod a real, writable, **empty** directory on the PVC — missing had become present-but-empty, with no skill loaded and nothing saying so. `prepareClaudePromptBundle` now takes `podDataMountPath`/`serverDataMountPath` and derives the server write path from the pod path it is given (`toServerAddress`, the same arithmetic `resolveLinkedWorktreeCommonDir` already uses), rather than taking two roots and trusting the caller to keep them in agreement — one construction site, translated, so the pair cannot drift. `ClaudePromptBundle` gains `serverRootDir` so the two address spaces are visible in the type instead of being a property a reader has to know. Also derives `resolvePromptCacheRoot`'s runtime-descriptor fallback from `resolveDataMountPath(config)` (it still hardcoded `/paperclip`, the same correction BLO-32734 applied to the other five), and exports `resolveDataMountPath`. **Seven guards, each separately mutation-tested** — reverting any one alone turns the suite red; the `addDir` writable-mount candidate needed a `promptCacheRoot: ""` (runtime-descriptor) fixture before it had a failing mutation at all, because under a config-source root `addDir` is a redundant descendant and the first fixture passed with the candidate deleted. A deliberately-absent `podMount === serverMount` fast path is called out in-comment: the arithmetic already yields the identity there, so such a branch would be documentation wearing a guard's clothes. No-op control retained and required — default mount emits byte-identical paths, and the `roots config-source isolation at the mount the pod actually has` test from #1820 passes unchanged. **Known residual, filed separately as [BLO-37961](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-37961): the bundle's skill entries are absolute SYMLINKS**, and a catalog-backed one targets `<PAPERCLIP_HOME>/instances/<id>/skills/<companyId>/__runtime__/<name>` — a server address with no pod counterpart, so under a custom mount those links dangle in the pod even with this fix in. Bundled `/app/skills/...` entries are image paths and are unaffected. Its writer is `resolveManagedSkillsRoot` in `server/src/services/company-skills.ts`, outside this adapter. **So this commit does not by itself make a custom `workspaceMountPath` work** — it fixes the addressing of the bundle, not of what the bundle points at. |
| [BLO-37760](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-37760) | `src/server/prompt-cache.ts`, `src/server/prompt-cache.test.ts` | Ally review of [#2107](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2107) (Important): the "not under the pod mount" early return in `toServerAddress` served two conditions with opposite meanings. The WRITE is correct in both (a server-side root is left untranslated), but the container is still handed that root as `--add-dir`, and it is not on the pod's data mount, so the bundle is absent or empty in the pod. That is the managed `PAPERCLIP_HOME` default under a custom `workspaceMountPath`, and it is also an operator-set `promptCacheRoot` that `resolvePromptCacheRoot` returns verbatim, which the derivation above cannot touch. Neither reached any report: `warnIfPersistentTreeIsOffVolume` only covers the three `storage`-gated roots, and `resolveScopedWritableMounts` only runs when narrowing is on. `prepareClaudePromptBundle` now emits `claude_k8s.prompt_bundle_off_volume` when the pod mount is known and the bundle root is not under it. Keyed on the pod mount alone, not on the two mounts differing: with them equal, an off-mount root is equally unreadable. Not `storage`-gated: the container is handed this path unconditionally, so there is no off-volume-by-design case. Warned, not thrown, on the `isolation_root_off_volume` precedent. Four tests; five mutants each turn the suite red (no warn; gate on `pod !== server`; warn only when under neither mount; warn whenever the pod mount is known; warn when the mount is unknown). |
| [BLO-37961](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-37961) | `src/server/prompt-cache.ts`, `src/server/prompt-cache.test.ts` | BLO-37760 above makes the prompt bundle's *directory* resolve from both address spaces; it does not fix what the directory **contains**. Each entry in `.claude/skills/` is an absolute symlink, and a catalog-backed skill's `source` arrives from a server service (`resolveManagedSkillsRoot`) as a **SERVER** address — but a symlink's target is resolved by whoever follows it, which is the agent pod. Under a custom `workspaceMountPath` the pod has no `/paperclip`, so every catalog-backed skill was a link it could not follow: present, correctly named, and dangling, with nothing in the bundle saying so. Added `toPodAddress`, the inverse of `toServerAddress`, and applied it to the link **content** only. The live set is mixed, which is why it was not obvious — `/app/skills/...` entries are **image** paths, identical in both namespaces, and are deliberately left untouched (rewriting them onto the data volume would break the one set that works today). Also repairs a **stale** link: `bundleKey` is content-derived and the server's own mount does not move, so the first run after an operator adopts a custom mount lands on the pre-existing bundle, where `ensurePaperclipSkillSymlink`'s "target still stat()s" fast path stats the old server address *here*, in server space, finds it, and keeps a link the pod cannot follow. Measured before fixing. Identity transform when the mounts coincide, so every emitted target is byte-identical on the default deployment (41/41 live agent Jobs measured 2026-09-29). `claude-local` is structurally unaffected: its `prepareClaudePromptBundle` takes no mount parameter and the adapter has one address space. All four guards separately mutation-tested per [BLO-34263](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-34263). |
| [BLO-37961](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-37961) | `src/server/prompt-cache.ts`, `src/server/prompt-cache.test.ts` | Ally review of [#2114](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2114) (Important): `toPodAddress`'s "not under the server mount" early return served two conditions with opposite meanings, the same shape Ally raised on `toServerAddress` in [#2107](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2107). It is correct for an IMAGE path (`/app/skills/...`), but a catalog-backed source is `resolveManagedSkillsRoot` under `PAPERCLIP_HOME`, while the server mount is `SELF_POD_DATA_MOUNT_PATH`: two variables that coincide today, not one. Where they diverge the source falls through untranslated and the pod gets a dangling link, and `prompt_bundle_off_volume` covers the bundle root only. `prepareClaudePromptBundle` now emits `claude_k8s.prompt_bundle_skill_off_volume` when the pod mount is known, the entry is catalog-backed (`catalogBackedSkillKeys`, same `?? true` default as `buildClaudePromptBundleKey`), and the link target is not under the pod mount. Keyed on the pod mount alone, per the #2107 precedent, and deliberately NOT on "`toPodAddress` returned it unchanged": with equal mounts that is the identity for every entry, including followable ones. Warned, not thrown. Three tests; six mutants each turn the suite red (no warn; gate on `pod !== server`; drop the catalog discriminator; warn whenever the pod mount is known; warn when `toPodAddress` returned the source unchanged; default omitted keys to non-catalog). |
| [BLO-38518](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-38518) | `src/server/execute.ts`, `src/server/prompt-cache.ts`, `src/server/prompt-cache.test.ts` | Ally review of [#2107](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2107) at `88129df3`, the head that rebase-merges #2114 into this branch. **(Important)** The comment heading the prompt-bundle block in `execute()` still asserted the single-address invariant this series exists to remove — *"the K8s Job pod mounts the same PVC at /paperclip, so bundle paths written here are accessible inside the pod at the identical absolute path"* — and was contradicted 39 lines below it, inside the same function, by the `rootDir` comment this series added. One function carrying both the claim and its refutation, with the false one first and unqualified, at the call site a reader is most likely to trust. Rewritten to name both mounts, the same correction `resolvePromptCacheRoot`'s doc comment already applies one function up. **(Suggestion)** The stale-link repair's `fs.unlink(target).catch(() => {})` was an indiscriminate swallow of the one failure that silently restores the defect the block exists to fix: on anything but ENOENT the stale link survives, `ensurePaperclipSkillSymlink` stats its old SERVER address, finds it, and returns `skipped`. Nothing reported it — in the migration shape `desired` IS under the pod mount, so `prompt_bundle_skill_off_volume` does not fire, and the enclosing `try/catch` never saw a throw because the rejection was already absorbed. Narrowed to ENOENT; any other error emits `claude_k8s.prompt_bundle_stale_skill_link_retained`. Two tests, with a negative control (no stale link ⇒ no warn) so the guard cannot pass on a warn emitted unconditionally; reverting the narrowing turns the suite red. **(Suggestion)** `withVolume` materializes the skill tree under both mounts, so the `fs.stat` clause in the first symlink test passes only because the fixture created the pod-side copy — in production `podDataMountPath` does not exist in server space at all. Harmless (`fs.symlink` never stats its source, so no guard is weakened) but noted in-test so a future reader does not take it as evidence the target resolves server-side. **Known residual, not fixed here:** `instructionsFilePath` is a SERVER address (`execute.ts` reads it with `fs.readFile` in this process) and is interpolated into the `pathDirective` prose appended to `instructionsContents`, which the bundle then materializes for the pod — so under a custom `workspaceMountPath` the agent is told to resolve relative references from a directory that is not a mount in its own pod. Same family as the rows above, one layer up: prose, not a path the runtime resolves, and latent at the default mount where the two addresses coincide. Tracked on [BLO-37961](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-37961), which the rows above otherwise describe as closed. |
